images.title: Square cut into L-shapes
images.purpose: Show a square dot grid split into nested L-shaped layers of 1, 3, 5 and 7 dots.
images.composition: One large 4 by 4 dot grid centred, with the four layer counts listed in a short column on the right.
images.exact_structure: One square grid of 4 by 4 dots, 16 dots in all, evenly spaced and equal in size. Four nested L-shaped layers from the top-left corner: 1 dot teal #0072B2, 3 dots amber #E69F00, 5 dots reddish purple #CC79A7, 7 dots grey #6B7280. Grey thin outlines mark each L. Four short count labels, one beside each layer. Exactly 1 grid.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
layers that overlap, or an L with a different dot count from its label
images.takeaway: A square grid splits into L-shaped layers of 1, 3, 5, 7 dots.
images.description: A 4 by 4 dot grid cut into four L-shaped layers coloured teal, amber, purple and grey with 1, 3, 5 and 7 dots.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to trace each L with a finger and say how many dots it holds.

image_decisions.why: One large grid with its layers is the cleanest way to see the odd-number partition.
